name: Requisition Raid
oracle_text:
Spree (Choose one or more additional costs.)
+ {1} — Destroy target artifact.
+ {1} — Destroy target enchantment.
+ {1} — Put a +1/+1 counter on each creature target player controls.
blocked_sentences: + {1} — Put a +1/+1 counter on each creature target player controls.

needs.what: a target spec owned by a spree mode (e.g. a `spree_mode: n` key on a card-level target), declared at 601.2c only when that mode was bought at 601.2b, so a cast line per spree subset enumerates the shared targets plus the targets of every chosen mode, and a mode whose required target is missing withdraws only the subsets containing it
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `spree` plus `if {spree_mode: n}` handles the priced modes but has no way to scope a target to a mode. A target spec's `mode` key needs a top-level `choose_mode` (resolution-time, not a cost); `cost_option` is refused without `additional_cost_options`, which the loader refuses beside `spree` and which is exclusive (one tier, never a subset). Declaring all three targets unconditionally would demand an artifact, an enchantment and a player on every cast and block the artifact-only mode when no enchantment exists; making them `optional` would let a cast that bought a mode skip its target, or target things for modes not bought
